LESSON: CONSERVING LIGHT ENVIRONMENT SCHOOL

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Care for the 3.4 Caring for water By the end of the sub-strand,  Learners to id
Topic 3.5: Conserving Light environment School

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Conserving Light environment School. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONSERVING LIGHT ENVIRONMENT SCHOOL
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Conserving Light environment School helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CONSERVING LIGHT ENVIRONMENT SCHOOL
Conserving Light environment School is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Conserving Light environment School” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Conserving Light environment School is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Conserving Light environment School” around your school. (skill: demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Conserving Light environment School to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Conserving Light environment School from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Conserving Light environment School: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Conserving Light environment School?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Conserving Light environment School means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate correct ways of using learners to discuss ways of light energy in the home and school saving light energy.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
